You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Input is an array of 3x3 colored glyph panels separated by blank rows; columns 0-2 are the left panel column and 4-6 the right panel column, with vertical color-4 divider at col 7. Output has same height and width 7. Move color-5 marker from input right area to output col = input marker col - 8 (examples: input marker c9->output c1; c11->c3; c12->c4). Read glyphs in column-major order: all left panels top-to-bottom, then all right panels top-to-bottom (not row-wise pairs). Each glyph maps to a directed straight stroke: color-1 pattern [[1,1,0],[1,0,1],[0,1,0]] => 3 cells horizontally right; color-2 [[2,0,2],[2,0,2],[2,2,2]] => 2 cells horizontally left; color-6 [[6,0,6],[0,6,0],[0,6,0]] => 2 cells vertically down; color-3 [[3,3,3],[0,3,0],[3,0,3]] => 4 cells horizontally left. Begin first stroke one row below marker at the same column. For every subsequent stroke, begin one row below the previous stroke’s endpoint, at that endpoint’s column; draw its cells including that start cell along its mapped direction. Repeated vertical strokes concatenate naturally. Leave remaining grid cells zero. This yields a continuous descending chain, with stroke colors and lengths as above. Validated against all 3 demos and test submission (correct).', global_=True)
